Zywiec Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Żywiec, Poland

Not demolished. Żywiec's Jewish settlement developed under the De Non-Tolerandis Judaeis restriction, in force from 1626, with an independent community, Żywiec-Zabłocie, established only in 1864. This cemetery, already in use by 1853, holds the matzevah of Walter Munk, a second lieutenant of artillery who served in both the Imperial and Royal Army and the Polish Army, posthumously awarded the Virtuti Militari for his defense of Zamość. During WWII, the Germans used significant quantities of the cemetery's matzevot to regulate a nearby stream; others, including the marble tombstone of Rabbi Nachman Hirsch Bau, were stolen after the war. In spring 1941, all of Żywiec's Jews were transported to the Sucha Beskidzka Ghetto, and most were later deported to Auschwitz-Birkenau.
